newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to ease stance on Eurobond buyers rule-sources.
newsitem.headline: MOF to ease stance on Eurobond buyers rule-sources.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) has softened a plan to require strict identification of investors in Eurobonds issued by Japanese firms, industry sources said on Tuesday.
The MOF has acknowledged the difficulty of requiring all investors to identify themselves and is showing flexibility in its most recent plan, the sources said.

MOF plans to adopt a rule on buyers being identified by April 1998 so as to close a loophole that has allowed Japanese investors to avoid tax on purchases of Euroyen bonds issued by Japanese, an official at MOF's Tax Bureau told Reuters.
Japan gives a tax break on income gains on foreign bonds issued by Japanese but held by non-residents of Japan.
A MOF study showed that about 70 to 80 percent of such bonds are held by Japanese investors.
The tax break is due to expire on March 31, 1998.
MOF has said the tax break was supposed to encourage bond purchases by foreigners but had been abused and that it would scrap it and demand strict identification of bond buyers.
But Japanese companies, financial institutions, brokers and Swiss banks have opposed the move, saying strict identification requirements would undermine foreign bond issues by Japanese.
As a result, the MOF is considering a softer approach.
"We are considering coming up with various ways to identify buyers on a case-by-case basis," the official said.
The MOF official said the ministry had already met with officials at various industries to discuss a compromise, but had yet to receive feedback.
Unlike other countries, Japan does not have any rules concerning identification of buyers and the MOF is trying to set up a system to meet global standards, the official said.
